question_text: According to the course material, the two main wind systems controlling Nigeria's climate are the South West Trade Winds and:
explanation: Nigeria's climate is controlled by two wind systems: the cool, dry North East Trade Winds (bringing harmattan dust) and the warm, moist South West Trade Winds (bringing cloud and rain).

question_text: According to the course material, one of Nigeria's worst air disasters occurred at Aminu Kano International Airport on 22nd January 1973 when a Jordanian airline crashed after harmattan haze reduced visibility to only 300 metres, killing:
explanation: On 22nd January 1973, harmattan haze reduced visibility to only 300 metres at Aminu Kano International Airport, and a Jordanian airline crashed, killing 176 people.

question_text: According to the course material, the highest rates of coastal erosion cited, driven by South West Trade Wind waves between June and October, occur at:
option_a: Bar Beach on Victoria Island, Lagos (25 to 30m per year)
option_c: Ibeno Eket in Akwa Ibom State (25 to 30m per year)
option_d: Forcados in the Niger Delta (25 to 30m per year)
explanation: Among the coastal erosion rates cited, Bar Beach on Victoria Island, Lagos experiences the highest rate at 25 to 30 metres per year, posing a serious disaster threat to the significant investment located there.

question_text: According to the course material, the Bagauda Dam, which burst in 1988 sweeping away villages, farmlands, and killing many people and livestock, was an example of damage caused by:
explanation: The Bagauda Dam collapse in 1988, which swept away villages and farmlands and killed many people and livestock, is cited as an example of the destructive impact of Nigeria's thunderstorms.

question_text: According to the course material, the 1980 flooding of the Ogunpa river in Ibadan, caused by a heavy downpour, resulted in about how many people drowned and how many rendered homeless?
explanation: In 1980, the Ogunpa river in Ibadan rose and covered about 6 sq. km. as a result of a heavy downpour; some 200 people were drowned and 30,000 were rendered homeless.

question_text: According to the course material, severe drought in Nigeria in 1972-1973 resulted in crop yields dropping in the most affected areas by between 60% and 78%, and approximately how many animals perishing?
explanation: The severe drought of 1972-1973 caused crop yields to drop by 60% to 78% in the most affected areas, and about 300,000 animals perished as a result.
